current_scene.title: The Tin Woodman’s Crossing
current_scene.text:
The Tin Woodman stood waiting on the other side of the gulf, and I bent down so that he might climb upon my back. His metal body was heavy, but I set my paws firmly on the ground and carried him toward the opening.

The gulf still frightened me. I could see the far bank beyond it, where Dorothy, Toto, and the Scarecrow waited, but my legs trembled as I reached the edge. I went on, holding the Tin Woodman securely, and crossed over to the others.

When my paws touched the far bank, I lowered myself and let the Tin Woodman climb down. Dorothy and Toto were safe beside the Scarecrow, and now all four travelers and Toto stood together on the far side of the first gulf.

I was too tired to go farther. After carrying the Tin Woodman across, I sat down upon the ground and rested, while my companions remained near me on the road.

entry_source:
They found the forest very thick on this side, and it looked dark and gloomy.
After the Lion had rested they started along the road of yellow brick, silently
wondering, each in his own mind, if ever they would come to the end of the
woods and reach the bright sunshine again. To add to their discomfort, they
soon heard strange noises in the depths of the forest, and the Lion whispered
to them that it was in this part of the country that the Kalidahs lived.
“What are the Kalidahs?” asked the girl.
“They are monstrous beasts with bodies like bears and heads like
tigers,” replied the Lion, “and with claws so long and sharp that
they could tear me in two as easily as I could kill Toto. I’m terribly
afraid of the Kalidahs.”
“I’m not surprised that you are,” returned Dorothy.
“They must be dreadful beasts.”
The Lion was about to reply when suddenly they came to another gulf across the
road. But this one was so broad and deep that the Lion knew at once he could
not leap across it.
So they sat down to consider what they should do, and after serious thought the
Scarecrow said:

rejected_transition.text:
After I had rested, we started along the yellow brick road through the thick, dark forest. Strange noises came from the trees, and I whispered that this was where the Kalidahs lived. When Dorothy asked what they were, I told her they were monstrous beasts with bodies like bears and heads like tigers, and admitted that I was terribly afraid of them.

Before I could say more, we came to another gulf across the road, too broad and deep for me to leap. We sat down to consider what we should do. Then the Scarecrow pointed out a great tree standing beside the gulf and suggested that, if the Tin Woodman chopped it down, it could fall across the gap and make a bridge. The Woodman’s axe was available, and the tree stood ready beside the gulf.

storyMemory.summary: After resting, I traveled with Dorothy, Toto, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman along the yellow brick road through a thick, gloomy forest. I warned them about the Kalidahs and admitted my fear. We reached a second, broader gulf that I cannot leap across. The Scarecrow proposed using a great tree beside it as a bridge, and the Tin Woodman’s axe is available for the task.
